conversation:
maya: Quick sync — customer (FinEdge) wants an EU-only POC next week. They require all inference traffic and logs to stay in EU, no cross-border egress. What's our current routing guarantee for Hosted vs Dedicated? Any short checklist I can share with them? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sam: Short answer: Hosted has regional endpoints and we can prefer eu-west endpoints, but Hosted can still touch sub-processors outside EU for some control-plane operations (audit logs ingestion, metrics). Dedicated = stronger guarantees — can be set up in EU-only capacity with VPC and optional on-prem control plane. I'll paste a config snippet.

sam: ```yaml
routing:
  preferred_region: eu-west-1
  enforce_tenant_pin: true
  egress: eu-only
  fallback: reject
``` 

maya: Helpful — they asked about sub-processors list & timeline for providing attestation docs (DD & SCC). Can we confirm exact subprocessors for EU hosted today and whether we can get POA from ops/legal?

liam: For Hosted EU: infra sub-processors = AWS eu-west-1, Datadog (metrics EU regional shard), Sentry (EU shard only for PII scrubbed), and ProviderX for observability (has EU contracts). Non-EU control-plane services are limited but exist (analytics batch jobs). If customer needs full sub-processor isolation, we recommend Dedicated or Private.

liam: I'll attach current subproc inventory link: https://redwood.example.com/subproc-inventory#eu

carla: Legal note — we can provide SCCs + subproc list for sales POCs, but full attestation (signed SOC-type evidence) takes ~3-4 weeks. For Dedicated, we can scope BYOK and KMS in-customer region. If they need contract language for data localization, escalate via me.

maya: Great. Pricing / POC logistics: customer asked whether EU-only Dedicated POC has a premium and what min commit looks like.

sam: POC pricing options: (1) short-term Dedicated trial (1–2 weeks) — we have an internal credit program but requires ops signoff for capacity; (2) Hosted with routing preferences — cheaper but not certified EU-only; (3) Private (on-prem) — highest work. I'll ping infra for capacity check.

ops-bot: Capacity request submitted (ticket #INC-8892). ETA for EU Dedicated warmup: 72 hours once approved.

maya: Can someone confirm what the runtime does on routing failure? If eu-west capacity is saturated and fallback is allowed, does it ever go to non-EU? We need explicit language for the caller.

liam: If your policy equals `fallback: reject` (see config), we will reject requests when EU capacity unavailable. If policy = `fallback: nearest`, then we may route to compatible non-EU model variant in a different region. Defaults are per-tenant; for POC we can set to reject.

maya: Perfect — I'll send the short checklist to the customer. Checklist draft (doable?):
- Choose Dedicated EU cluster or Hosted (note limitations)
- Provide security questionnaire + PO contact
- Confirm KMS/BYOK need
- Approve fallback policy (reject vs nearest)
- Sign POC scope (ops capacity & timeline)

sam: That looks good. Add: confirm allowed sub-processors and expected SLA for the POC.

maya: I'll send that, attach the subproc link and sampler config. TY everyone :handshake:
